note: Week 6 · THE TITANS WON A FOOTBALL GAME
lede: THE TITANS WON. Three hundred and one days since the last one. Zero and five, seven straight losses, eleven straight inside the division, thirteen points down at halftime in Indianapolis with sixty-four yards of offense to their name — and then they scored twenty-six unanswered and walked out of Lucas Oil Stadium with it. At halftime the Colts honored Adam Vinatieri at midfield and he told the building it was a bad day to be a Titan. Reader, it was not.

beats.text: They were outgained 399 to 186. They lost the ball-control battle by seventeen minutes. They had eleven first downs. NONE OF IT MATTERED. Chimere Dike returned a punt 58 yards and Cam Ward found Carnell Tate from eight for the rookie's first career touchdown. Four minutes later Julius Chestnut and James Williams came through the line, the punt went nowhere, and Femi Oladejo scooped it off the turf and ran fourteen yards into the end zone — Tennessee's first blocked-punt return touchdown since 2011 and the first one anybody has scored in the NFL this season. Taylor tied it. Joey Slye untied it from 49 with 2:03 left and salted it from 44 with 0:43. Fourth-and-seventeen, incomplete, ballgame.

Six sacks, a season high, and three takeaways. Jeffery Simmons had two of the sacks, six tackles, a forced fumble AND the recovery, passed Ted Washington for tenth on the franchise sack list, and — per ESPN — gave the halftime speech that turned the thing. Amani Hooker had a career-high thirteen tackles and picked off Daniel Jones at the Indianapolis six. Cor'Dale Flott got another at the eleven. Robert Saleh has his first win as head coach, and the franchise has its 500th all time. They were seven-point underdogs.

And the Titans were only a quarter of it. Pittsburgh came back from 16-3 down and won in overtime on a Rodgers screen to Germie Bernard, who caught eleven balls. Kansas City handled the Chargers 22-6 and is 5-0. Buffalo went into Las Vegas and beat Mark 33-30 — Josh Allen tied Jim Kelly's franchise record of 258 career touchdown passes on a backhanded flip, Cook ran in the winner, and the Bills recovered the onside kick to end it. Four teams, four wins, third sweep anyone has managed this season and the first since Mark in Week 3.

The empire has one point with a game still to play. Chicago beat Atlanta behind Caleb Williams going 30-of-36 in his first game back from the hamstring, and that was all of it — Cleveland beat Baltimore 13-10 on a last-second field goal with Lamar Jackson out again, and Las Vegas lost to Jon. A four-point lead is down to one. Which means tonight, for the first time all season, seven owners sit down to root hard for Harrison's 1-3-1 Commanders, a team not one of them would otherwise think about.

beats.tag: Zach · On the board, at Bill's expense
beats.text: Green Bay beat Dallas 23-13 on Sunday night and Zach finally has something. The Packers led wire to wire and converted their first seven third downs; Dak Prescott threw interceptions on back-to-back second-quarter drives, both inside the Green Bay 30, and Dallas went scoreless in a first half for the first time since 2021. Kenny Clark, sent to Dallas in the Micah Parsons trade, got his first sack of the season — at Lambeau, against the team that traded him. Zach is up to six. Bill, who had the other side of it, finishes 0/3 and is the only owner blanked this week.
